B *Commentary*
B1 Duke Hui's primary wife was Mengzi.
After Mengzi died,
she was succeeded by Shengzi as his secondary wife,
who gave birth to Duke Yin.
Duke Wu of Song gave birth to Zhongzi.
When Zhongzi was born, there was a mark on her hand
that said, "She will be the Lady of Lu,"
therefore, Zhongzi was sent to us [Lu].
She gave birth to Duke Huan, and Duke Hui died,
therefore, Duke Yin was established [as ruler] and served her [Zhongzi].
A1.1 *Annals of Duke Yin, Year 1*
A1.1.1 In the first year, in spring, the king's first month.
A1.1.2 In the third month,
the Duke and Yi Fu of Zhu made a covenant at Mie.
A1.1.3 In summer, the fifth month,
the Earl of Zheng overcame Duan at Yan.
A1.1.4 In autumn, the seventh month,
the King sent Zai Xuan to return the gifts for Duke Hui and
Zhongzi's burial.
A1.1.5 In the ninth month,
(Duke Yin) and the people of Song made a covenant at Su.
A1.1.6 In the twelfth month of winter,
Ji Bo came.
A1.1.7 Gongzi Yishi died.
B1.1 *The Commentary to the First Year of Duke Yin*
B1.1.1 In the first year, in the spring,
the royal Zhou first month,
his enthronement was not recorded,
because he was acting as regent.
B1.1.2 In the third month,
the Duke and Yi Fu of Zhu made a covenant at Mie.
He was Ke, the Viscount of Zhu.
Because it was not by royal command,
his rank was not recorded.
He is called "Yi Fu"
to show respect to him.
Because the Duke was acting as regent and wished to seek amity with Zhu,
therefore he made the covenant at Mie.
B1.1.3 In the fourth month of summer,
Fei Bo led troops to fortify Lang.
It was not recorded,
because it was not by the Duke's order.
B1.1.4 Initially,
Duke Wu of Zheng married a woman from Shen,
named Wu Jiang.
She gave birth to Duke Zhuang and Gongshu Duan.
Duke Zhuang was born feet first (lit., born waking),
which startled Lady Jiang.
Therefore, he was named Wusheng (lit., Awoken at Birth),
and consequently, she disliked him.
She loved Gongshu Duan
and wanted to establish him as the heir.
She frequently pleaded with Duke Wu,
but the Duke did not permit it.
When Duke Zhuang ascended the throne,
she requested the fief of Zhi for him.
The Duke said,
"Zhi
is a fortified city;
Guo Shu died there.
Other cities, I will grant according to decree."
She requested Jing
and had him reside there,
calling him Grand Uncle of Jingcheng.
Ji Zhong said,
"A capital city
exceeding one hundred *zhi* in circumference
is a danger to the state.
The regulations of the former kings are:
a large capital city
should not exceed one-third the size of the state;
Middle,
one-fifth;
small,
one-ninth.
Now, the capital exceeding the limit,
is not in accordance with the regulations,
your Lordship will not be able to endure it."
The Duke said:
"Jiang desires it,
how can I avoid harming her?"
He replied:
"How can Jiang ever be satisfied?
It is better to make provisions for him early,
do not allow it to spread!
Once it spreads,
it will be difficult to deal with.
Even spreading weeds cannot be removed,
how much more so your Lordship's favored younger brother?"
The Duke said:
"One who commits many injustices will surely bring about his own downfall,
you just wait and see."
Later, Uncle commanded the western and northern borders to be disloyal to the Duke and loyal to himself.
Gongzi Lü said:
"The state cannot bear disloyalty,
what will your Lordship do?
If you intend to give it to Uncle,
I request to serve him;
if you do not give it to him,
then please remove him,
so as not to stir the people's hearts."
The Duke said,
"No need,
he will bring it upon himself."
The Grand Uncle further seized Er as his own city,
reaching as far as Lin Yan.
Zi Feng said,
"It is permissible.
Great generosity will win over the masses."
The Duke said,
"It is unrighteous,
and does not foster affection.
Great generosity will lead to collapse."
The Grand Uncle fortified and amassed resources,
repaired armor and weapons,
prepared soldiers and chariots,
intending to attack Zheng.
The Lady was going to open the gates for him.
The Duke heard of the planned date,
and said,
"It is permissible."
He ordered Zi Feng to lead two hundred chariots to attack Jing.
Jing rebelled against Grand Uncle Duan.
Duan fled into Yan.
The Duke attacked him at Yan.
On the Xin Chou day of the fifth month,
Grand Uncle fled to Gong.
The *Book of Documents* says:
"The Earl of Zheng conquered Duan at Yan."
Duan was not a good younger brother,
therefore, it does not say "younger brother";
treating them as two rulers,
therefore it says "conquered";
calling him "Earl of Zheng,"
criticizes his failure to teach (his brother);
this is called the Zheng record.
It does not say "fled,"
because it was difficult to say so.
Then he placed Lady Jiang in the city of Ying,
and swore an oath to her, saying:
"Until we reach the Yellow Springs,
we shall not see each other!"
Afterwards, he regretted it.
Ying Kao-shu was the border official of Ying Valley.
Hearing of this,
he made an offering to the duke.
The duke gave him food.
He left the meat uneaten.
The duke asked him about it.
He replied:
"I, a humble man, have a mother,
who has always tasted my food;
she has never tasted the duke's soup,
I beg to give it to her."
The duke said:
"You have a mother to leave behind,
but I alone have none!"
Ying Kao Shu said:
"May I venture to ask what you mean?"
The Duke told him the reason
and also told him of his regret.
He replied:
"What does Your Lordship have to worry about?
If you dig a tunnel reaching to the spring,
and meet her through it,
who would say it is not right?"
The Duke followed his advice.
The Duke entered and recited:
"Within the great tunnel,
the joy is harmonious."
Jiang came out and recited:
"Outside the great tunnel,
the joy is overflowing."
Thereupon, they became as mother and son as before.
The gentleman said:
"Ying Kao Shu
was truly filial.
He loved his mother
and extended that love to Duke Zhuang.
The *Book of Poetry* says:
'A filial son is never deficient;
he will forever bestow blessings on your kind.'
That is what this refers to!"
B1.1.5 In the seventh month of autumn,
the King of Heaven sent the steward Xuan to bring the gifts (賵) for Duke Hui and Zhongzi.
It was slow (緩),
and furthermore, the Zi clan woman had not yet died,
therefore they are named.
The Son of Heaven is buried in the seventh month,
and those who share the same tracks (同軌, i.e., those under his direct administration) all arrive;
the feudal lords in the fifth month,
and those of the same alliance (同盟) arrive;
the grand officers in the third month,
and those of the same rank (同位) arrive;
the officers after a month,
and relatives by marriage (外姻) arrive.
To make gifts for the dead before the body is present,
to express condolences to the living before mourning begins,
and to anticipate calamitous events
is contrary to propriety.
B1.1.6 In the eighth month,
the people of Ji attacked the Yi.
The Yi did not report it,
therefore it was not recorded.
B1.1.7 There were locusts (蜚).
Because they did not cause disaster,
it also was not recorded.
B1.1.8 In the later years of Duke Hui,
he defeated the Song army at Huang.
After the Duke (Yin) ascended (to the throne), he sought peace.
In the ninth month,
In the ninth month,
(our lord) and the men of Song made a covenant at Su,
and intercourse (between the states) began.
B1.1.9 In the tenth month, on the day Gengshen,
they reburied Duke Hui.
The Duke did not attend,
therefore it is not recorded.
At the time of Duke Hui's death,
there were Song troops (present),
and the heir apparent was young,
so the burial was deficient.
Therefore, they reburied him.
B1.1.10 The Marquis of Wei came to attend the funeral,
but did not see the Duke,
so it is also not recorded.
B1.1.11 In the Zheng Gongshu Rebellion,
Gongsun Hua fled to Wei.
The men of Wei attacked Zheng on his behalf,
and took Linyan.
The men of Zheng, with the king's army and
the Guo army, attacked the southern border of Wei.
He requested troops from Zhu.
The Viscount of Zhu employed someone to privately petition Gongzi Yu.
Yu requested to go,
but the Duke did not permit it.
He then went,
and he and the men of Zhu and
the men of Zheng made a covenant at Yi.
Not recorded,
because it was not by the duke's command.
B1.1.12 The new construction of the south gate,
not recorded,
also because it was not by the duke's command.
B1.1.13 In the twelfth month,
the sacrificial envoy Bo came,
not by the king's command.
B1.1.14 When Zhongfu died,
the duke did not participate in the small encoffining,
therefore the date was not recorded.
A1.2 *Duke Yin, Year 2 Chronicle*
A1.2.1 In the second year, spring,
the duke met with the Rong people at Qian.
A1.2.2 In summer, the fifth month,
the people of Ju entered Xiang.
A1.2.3 Wu Hai led an army to enter Ji.
A1.2.4 In autumn, the eighth month, on the day Gengchen,
the duke and the Rong made an alliance at Tang.
A1.2.5 In the ninth month,
Ji Liexu came to escort the daughter.
A1.2.6 In winter, the tenth month,
Bo Ji was married to Ji.
A1.2.7 The Viscount of Ji and the Viscount of Ju made a covenant at Mi.
A1.2.8 In the twelfth month, on the day Yimao, Lady Zishi passed away.
A1.2.9 The people of Zheng attacked Wei.
B1.2 *The Commentary of the Second Year of Duke Yin*
B1.2.1 In the second year, in spring, the Duke met with the Rong at Qian, to renew the friendship of Duke Hui.
The Rong requested a covenant, but the Duke declined.
B1.2.2 The Viscount of Ju married from Xiang. Xiang Jiang was uneasy in Ju and returned.
In summer, the people of Ju entered Xiang, and brought back the Jiang woman.
B1.2.3 Sikong Wuhai entered Ji, and Fei Qin Fu defeated him.
B1.2.4 The Rong requested a covenant.
In autumn, they made a covenant at Tang, renewing the friendship with the Rong.
B1.2.5 In the ninth month, Ji Liexu came to escort the bride; a卿 *qing* official escorting on behalf of the ruler.
Ji Liexu came to meet the daughter (in marriage).
As a卿 (high minister), he met her on behalf of the ruler.
B1.2.6 In winter,
Viscount Bo of Ji
and the Viscount of Ju
formed an alliance at Mi,
because of Lu.
B1.2.7 The people of Zheng attacked Wei
to punish the rebellion of Gongsun Hua.
A1.3 *The Annals of Duke Yin, Year Three*
A1.3.1 In the spring of the third year, the king's second month,
on the day of Ji-si,
there was a solar eclipse.
A1.3.2 In the third month, on the day of Geng-xu,
the Heavenly King passed away.
A1.3.3 In the summer, the fourth month, on the day of Xin-mao,
the Lady of the Ruler passed away.
A1.3.4 In the autumn,
the son of the Wu lineage came seeking funeral contributions.
A1.3.5 In the eighth month, on the day of Geng-chen,
Duke Mu of Song, He, passed away.
A1.3.6 In the winter, the twelfth month,
The Marquis of Qi and
the Earl of Zheng formed an alliance at Shimen.
A1.3.7 On Guiwei
, the Duke Mu of Song was buried.
B1.3 *Zuo Zhuan*, Year 3 of Duke Yin
B1.3.1 In the spring of the third year,
in the third month of the king,
on Renxu,
King Ping died.
The report of his death arrived on Gengxu,
therefore it is recorded.
B1.3.2 In summer,
the Lady of the Ruler died.
-- This was the Lady Sheng.
There was no announcement of her death to the feudal lords,
no returning to the bedchamber to mourn,
and no spirit tablet placed with her husband's aunt,
therefore it is not said
"薨" (died, used for nobles).
She is not referred to as "夫人" (Lady),
therefore her burial is not mentioned,
and her surname is not written.
Because of the Duke's sake,
it is said
"the Lady of the Ruler".
B1.3.3 Duke Wu and Duke Zhuang of Zheng
served as ministers to King Ping.
The King showed favoritism to Guo.
The Earl of Zheng resented the King.
The King said,
"There is no such thing."
Therefore, Zhou and Zheng exchanged hostages.
Prince Hu of the King was a hostage in Zheng,
and Gongzi Hu of Zheng was a hostage in Zhou.
The King died.
The people of Zhou were about to give the government to the Duke of Guo.
In the fourth month,
Zheng Jizu led troops to take the wheat of Wen.
In the autumn,
he also took the grain of Chengzhou.
Zhou and Zheng became enemies.
A gentleman said:
"If trust does not come from within,
hostages are of no benefit.
If one acts with understanding and forgiveness,
and regulates conduct with propriety,
even without hostages,
who can sow discord?
If there is genuine trust,
even the fur from streams, brooks,
ponds, and islets,
the duckweed, white artemisia,
and pondweed from swamps,
Baskets, hampers,
tripods, and cauldrons,
stagnant puddles, foul water,
and water flowing after rain,
can be offered to spirits,
and presented to kings and dukes.
How much more so when a gentleman establishes trust between two states
and conducts affairs with propriety,
what need is there for oaths?
The *Airs* contain "Gathering the White Artemisia"
and "Gathering the Duckweed,"
the *Odes* contain "Rows of Reeds"
and "Drawing from the Deep Well,"
which demonstrate loyalty and trustworthiness."
B1.3.4 A son of the Wu family came seeking aid for burial,
but the king had not yet been buried.
B1.3.5 Duke Mu of Song fell ill,
and summoned the Grand Marshal Kong Fu
to entrust the infant Duke Shang to him,
saying:
"The former lord abandoned Yu and Yi and established me,
which I dare not forget.
If by the spirits of the high officials
I can preserve my head and body until death,
should the former lord ask about Yu and Yi,
what excuse shall I use to answer?
I ask you to support him
and make him the master of the altars of the soil and grain.
Though I die,
I will have no regrets."
The ministers replied,
"Your servants wish to support Feng."
The Duke said,
"That cannot be.
The late ruler considered me virtuous
and appointed me to govern the state.
If I abandon virtue and do not yield,
it would be overturning the late ruler's decision.
How could I be called virtuous?
To brightly illuminate the late ruler's virtuous commands,
how can I not strive for that?
My sons, do not abandon the late ruler's accomplishments!"
He had Gongzi Feng go and reside in Zheng.
On the day Gengchen of the eighth month,
Duke Mu of Song died,
and Duke Shang took the throne.
A gentleman said,
"Duke Xuan of Song can be said to have known men well.
He established Duke Mu,
and his son enjoyed (the benefits of it).
His appointment was indeed righteous!
The *Shang Song* says,
'Yin received the mandate and was entirely suitable;
it bore the hundred blessings.'
Is it not referring to this!"
B1.3.6 In winter,
Qi and Zheng formed an alliance at Shimen,
which was a continuation of the alliance at Lu.
On the day of Gengxu,
the carriage of the Count of Zheng overturned in the Ji River.
B1.3.7 Duke Zhuang of Wei married the younger sister of Minister Dechen of the Qi Eastern Palace,
named Zhuang Jiang,
who was beautiful but had no children.
The people of Wei composed the "Shuo Ren" (Ode to the Tall and Handsome Lady) for her.
He also married a woman from Chen,
named Li Gui,
who gave birth to Xiao Bo,
who died young.
Her younger sister, Dai Gui,
gave birth to Duke Huan,
whom Zhuang Jiang considered her own son.
Gongzi (Lord) Zhou Yu
was the son of a concubine.
He was favored and loved military affairs,
but the Duke did not restrain him.
Zhuang Jiang detested him.
Shi Que advised,
"I have heard that if you love your son,
you should teach him with righteous principles,
and not let him fall into evil.
Arrogance, extravagance, licentiousness, and dissipation
are where evil comes from.
These four things arise
when favor and emoluments are excessive.
To establish Duke Zhou Xu,
he had already decided upon it.
If it still isn't right,
this will be the stepping stone to disaster.
Now, one who is favored but not arrogant,
arrogant but able to humble himself,
humbled but without resentment,
resentful but able to reflect,
is rare indeed.
Moreover, for the lowly to obstruct the noble,
the young to insult the old,
the distant to alienate the close,
the new to estrange the old,
the small to encroach upon the large,
and indulgence to destroy righteousness,
these are the so-called six rebellions.
The ruler being righteous,
the ministers acting accordingly,
the father being kind,
the son being filial,
the elder brother being loving,
the younger brother being respectful,
these are the so-called six obediences.
To abandon obedience and imitate rebellion
is how one hastens disaster.
A ruler,
whose duty it is to eliminate disaster,
yet hastens it,
Wouldn't that be unacceptable?"
He did not listen.
His son, Hou, associated with Zhou Yu.
He forbade it,
but it was not possible (to stop him).
When Duke Huan was established,
he retired.
A1.4 *Annals of Duke Yin, Year 4*
A1.4.1 In the fourth year, spring,
in the second month of the king,
The people of Ju attacked Qi,
and took Mou Lou.
A1.4.2 On the day of Wushen,
Zhou Yu of Wei murdered his lord, Wan.
A1.4.3 In summer,
the Duke met with the Duke of Song at Qing.
A1.4.4 The Duke of Song,
the Marquis of Chen,
the people of Cai,
and the people of Wei attacked Zheng.
A1.4.5 In autumn,
Hui led troops to join the Duke of Song,
the Marquis of Chen,
the people of Cai,
and the people of Wei to attack Zheng.
A1.4.6 In the ninth month,
the people of Wei killed Zhou Yu at Pu.
A1.4.7 In the twelfth month of winter,
the people of Wei installed Jin.
B1.4 *Commentary on the Fourth Year of Duke Yin*
B1.4.1 In the spring of the fourth year,
Zhou Yu of Wei murdered Duke Huan and established himself.
B1.4.2 The Duke held a meeting with the Duke of Song,
intending to renew the alliance of Su.
Before the appointed time arrived,
the people of Wei came to report the rebellion.
In summer,
the Duke (Yin) and the Duke of Song met in Qing.
B1.4.3 When Duke Shang of Song ascended the throne,
Gongzi Feng fled to Zheng.
The people of Zheng wanted to install him.
After Zhou Xu of Wei came to power,
he intended to avenge the former ruler's grievances against Zheng
and seek favor from the lords,
in order to pacify his people.
He sent a message to Song, saying:
"If Your Lordship attacks Zheng
to remove your enemy,
Your Lordship will be the leader,
and our humble state will provide resources and join with Chen and
Cai to follow.
This is the wish of the state of Wei."
The people of Song agreed to this.
There was a man from the state of Guo named Gongsun Youshan.
B12.27.5 In the fourth year of Duke Dao,
the Jin general Xun Yao led an army to besiege Zheng.
Before they arrived,
Zheng's Si Hong said,
"Zhi Bo is stubborn and loves to win.
If we submit to him early,
it will be feasible."
So he first fortified Nanli to await him.
Zhi Bo entered Nanli
and approached the gate of Jiezhi.
The people of Zheng captured Xukui Leilei,
bribed him with knowledge of the government,
sealed his mouth, and then killed him.
When Zhi Bo was about to enter the gate, he asked,
"Open it and let me in!"
The guard replied,
"The ruler is here."
Zhi Bo said,
"To be disliked and without courage,
how can you be considered a son?"
The guard replied,
"By being able to endure shame,
perhaps I can prevent harm to the Zhao lineage!"
Zhi Bo did not repent.
Zhao Xiangzi therefore harbored resentment towards Zhi Bo,
and ultimately destroyed him.
Zhi Bo was greedy and stubborn,
therefore Han
and Wei rebelled against him and caused his downfall.
it is not recorded in the records.
B1.11.8 Yu Fu requested to kill Duke Huan,
intending to seek the position of Grand Minister.
The Duke said,
"Because he is young,
I intend to bestow it upon him."
I will have him build Tuqiu,
and I will retire there."
Yu Fu was afraid,
and instead slandered the Duke to Duke Huan and requested to assassinate him.
When the Duke was a young master,
he fought with the people of Zheng at Huyang,
and stopped there.
The people of Zheng imprisoned him in the Yin family.
He bribed the Yin family,
and prayed to their master, the sorcerer Zhong Wu.
Then he returned with the Yin family,
and established their master.
In the eleventh month,
the Duke sacrificed to the sorcerer Zhong Wu,
prepared himself at the altar in the garden,
and lodged at the Wei family.
On the day of Ren Chen,
Yu Fu sent assassins to kill the Duke at the Wei family,
and established Duke Huan,
and punished the Wei family,
causing deaths.
There was no record of the burial,
It was not yet a proper mourning.
Huán Gōng
A2.1 *Huán Gōng Yuánnián Jīng*
A2.1.1 First Year, Spring,
The Marquis of Xi attacked Zheng.
The Earl of Zheng fought with him at the border,
and the Xi army was utterly defeated and returned.
This is how the gentleman knew that Xi was about to perish:
"Not assessing virtue,
not measuring strength,
is not intimate with his relatives,
does not verify his words,
and does not investigate the guilty.
He commits these five unrighteous acts
and uses them to attack others.
It is no surprise that he loses his army,
is it not fitting?"
B1.11.7 In the tenth month of winter,
the Count of Zheng, with the army of Guo, attacked Song.
On the day *renxu*,
he greatly defeated the Song army,
in order to avenge their entry into Zheng.
Song did not report this order,
therefore it was not recorded.
Whenever the feudal lords had an order,
if it was reported, it was recorded;
otherwise, it was not.
Whether an army is successful or not,
it is also the same.
Even regarding the destruction of a state,
if the vanquished does not report their defeat,
or the victor does not report their victory,
and punishments are for correcting evil.
Since he has neither virtuous governance
nor awe-inspiring punishments,
this is how he allows evil to flourish.
Having allowed evil to flourish, he then curses it;
what benefit will this bring?"
B1.11.5 King (Huan of Zhou) took the fields of Wu,
Liu, Wei,
and Yu from Zheng,
and gave the people of Zheng the fields of Su Fen-sheng:
Wen, Yuan,
Chi, Fan,
Xi Cheng,
Zuan Mao,
Xiang, Meng,
Zhou, Xing,
Tui, and Huai.
This is how the gentleman knew
that King Huan had lost Zheng.
To be forgiving and act accordingly
is the model of virtue,
the principle of propriety.
To not be able to possess something oneself
yet give it to others,
is it not fitting that people do not come [to support you]?
B1.11.6 Zheng and
Xi had conflicting words.
The royal house is already degraded.
The descendants of Zhou are daily losing their order.
Xu,
is a descendant of the Great Mountain.
If Heaven is already tired of the virtue of Zhou,
how can I contend with Xu?"
The gentleman said that Duke Zhuang of Zheng
"in this matter, he possessed ritual propriety.
Ritual propriety
manages the state,
stabilizes the altars of the soil and grain,
orders the people,
benefits future generations.
Xu
was attacked without being formally charged,
he conquered them and then released them,
he assessed his virtue and then took his position,
he measured his strength and then acted.
He moved in accordance with the times,
without burdening future generations;
he can be said to know ritual propriety."
B1.11.4 Duke Zheng ordered his soldiers to release a boar,
and lead out dogs
and chickens,
in order to curse those who shot Ying Kaoshu.
The gentleman said that Duke Zhuang of Zheng
"has lost his governance and punishments.
Governance is for ruling the people,
how dare I take Xu as my own merit?
I have a younger brother [Duke Duan of Gong],
who is unable to be harmonious and cooperative,
and has been forced to make a living in all four directions,
how could I possibly hold Xu for long?
May you, sir, uphold Xu,"
Shu in comforting and pacifying this people.
I will have Huo assist you.
If I should be buried in the ground,
may Heaven, according to ritual, avert misfortune from Xu.
Would it not be better for the current Lord of Xu to once again uphold his altars of soil and grain,
so that only my Zheng state would have requests to make of him,
as in the old days of marriage alliances,
if he could condescend to follow our lead.
Do not let other clans take root here and crowd this place,
to contend with my Zheng state for this land.
My descendants will not even have time to avoid ruin,
how much less will they be able to sacrifice to Xu?
My sending you to stay here,
is not only for the sake of Xu,
but also to strengthen my borders."
Thereupon, he sent Gongsun Huo to reside in the western part of Xu,
and said:
"All your implements, utensils, and wealth,
do not place them in Xu.
When I die,
then leave quickly!
My late lord established a new city here.
On the day Geng-chen,
they arrived near Xu.
Ying Kao Shu took the Earl of Zheng's flag (decorated with a) mao hu (蝥弧)
to be the first to climb the city wall,
Zi Du shot at him from below,
and he fell.
Xia Shuying then used the *maohu* to climb,
waved the Zhou banner and shouted,
"The ruler has ascended!"
The Zheng army all then climbed up.
On the day *renwu*,
they finally entered Xu.
Duke Zhuang of Xu fled to Wei.
The Marquis of Qi wanted to cede Xu to Duke Yin of Lu.
Duke Yin said,
"You, my lord, said that Xu was disobedient,
therefore I followed you to punish it.
Xu has already submitted to its punishment,
even if you, my lord, have an order,
I, your subject, dare not participate in it."
So he gave it to the people of Zheng.
The Zheng ruler ordered the Xu grand master Baili to escort Xu Shu
to reside in the eastern part of Xu,

[Bù yí], (If there is no doubt,)

B2.12.1 In the summer of the twelfth year,

Jǔ.
B2.12.2 The Duke wanted to make peace between Sòng and Zhèng.

B2.13.1 In the spring of the thirteenth year,
Qū Xiá of Chǔ attacked Luó,

and said,
"You must send reinforcements!"

"The Grand Master is probably not referring to the masses,
but rather is saying that you, my lord, should cherish the common people with trust,

bì Xiǎo Luó.

"Gāo Bó will probably be executed!

A2.18 *Huán Gōng 18th Year Classic*
A2.18.1 In the spring of the eighteenth year, the king's first month,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Qí at Luò.

A2.18.2 In the summer, the fourth month, on the day bǐng zǐ,

A2.18.3 On the day dīng yǒu,

A2.18.4 In the autumn, the seventh month.
A2.18.5 In the winter, the twelfth month, on the day jǐ chǒu,

B2.18 *Huán Gōng 18th Year Commentary*
B2.18.1 In the spring of the eighteenth year,
the Duke was about to travel,
and consequently went to Qí 齊 with Jiāng 姜.
Shēn Xū 申繻 said:
"A woman has her family,
a man has his household;
they should not violate each other.
This is called propriety.
To change this
will certainly lead to failure."
The Duke met with the Marquis of Qí 齊 at Luò 濼,
and consequently took Wén Jiāng 文姜 to Qí 齊.
The Marquis of Qí 齊 had illicit relations with her.
The Duke reproached her for it.
She informed the Marquis of Qí 齊.
In the fourth month, on the day bǐngzǐ 丙子,
he feasted the Duke.
He had Gōngzǐ Péngshēng 公子彭生 drive the Duke's carriage,
and the Duke died in the carriage.
The people of Lǔ 魯 reported to Qí 齊, saying:
"Our late lord, fearing Your Lordship's power,
did not dare to remain in peace,
and came to renew the old alliance.
The rites were completed, but he did not return;
there is no one to blame,
and this would be looked upon unfavorably by the various lords.
We ask that Péngshēng 彭生 be executed to appease them."
The people of Qí killed Péng Shēng.
B2.18.2 In autumn,
the Marquis of Qí encamped his troops at Shǒuzhǐ;
Zǐ Wěi met with him,
with Gāo Qúmí as his attendant.
On the day wùxū of the seventh month,
the people of Qí killed Zǐ Wěi,
and quartered Gāo Qúmí.
Jì Zhòng went to Chén to welcome the Zheng heir
and installed him.
On this journey,
Jì Zhòng was aware of it,
so he feigned illness and did not go.
People said:
"Jì Zhòng avoided it through his knowledge."
Zhòng said:
"Indeed."
B2.18.3 The Duke of Zhōu wanted to assassinate King Zhuāng
and install Prince Kè.
Xīn Bó informed the king,
and together with the king, they killed the Duke of Zhōu Hēi Jiān.
Prince Kè fled to Yān.
Initially,
Zǐ Yí was favored by King Huán,
and King Huán entrusted him to the Duke of Zhōu.
Xīn Bó advised, saying:
"Having two queens, matching consorts, dual governance, paired states,
is the root of disorder."
Zhōu Gōng did not follow it,
therefore it extended (to this point).

B3.4.1 In the fourth year, in spring, in the first month of the King, King Wǔ of Chǔ (Chǔ Wǔ Wáng) died in Jīng, and commanded his army to Jíe, in order to attack Suí. He was about to depart and entered to inform his wife, Dèng Màn, saying, "My heart is agitated." Dèng Màn sighed and said, "The King's fortune is exhausted. To be full and then agitated is the way of Heaven. The former ruler knew this; therefore, when about to engage in military affairs and issue a major command, he agitated the King's heart."
A3.4.6 In autumn, the seventh month.
A3.4.7 In winter, the Duke and the people of Qí (Qí) hunted at Zhuó.
To be full and then to overflow is
the way of Heaven.
Our late lord knew this.
Therefore, when facing military affairs
and about to issue a major command,
he made the king's heart overflow.
If the army and its followers suffer no loss,
and the king dies on the road,
it is a blessing for the state."
The king then proceeded
and died beneath the Mánmù trees.
The Lìngyǐn Dòu Qí and the Mò'áo Qū Zhòng
cleared the roads, bridged the Zhà River,

and sued for peace.

In the first month of the year,

B3.6 *Zuǒ Zhuàn*, Year 6 of Duke Zhuāng
B3.6.1 In the spring of the sixth year,
the king's men rescued Wèi.
In summer,
the Marquis of Wèi entered,
exiled Gōngzǐ Qiánmóu to Zhōu,
exiled Níng Guì to Qín,
killed Zuǒ Gōngzǐ Xiè and
Yòu Gōngzǐ Zhí,
and then ascended the throne.
The noble man considers the two lords' installation of Qiánmóu as without measure.
For one who can secure his position
must measure the beginning and the end,
Only then can one establish impartiality.
Without knowing the root,
one does not make plans;
knowing that the root will not branch out,
one does not force it.
The *Book of Poetry* says:
"The root and branches last for a hundred generations."
B3.6.2 In winter,
the people of Qí 齊 came to return the treasures of Wèi 衛,
at the request of Wén Jiāng 文姜.
B3.6.3 King Wén of Chǔ 楚文王 attacked Shēn 申.
He passed through Dèng 鄧.
The Marquis of Dèng 鄧祁侯 said:
"He is my nephew."
He stopped and feasted him.
Zhuī Shēng 騅甥, Dān Shēng 聃甥, and Yǎng Shēng 養甥
requested to kill the Chǔ 楚 ruler.
The Marquis of Dèng 鄧侯 did not allow it.
The three *shēng* said:
"The one who will destroy the state of Dèng 鄧 is
surely this man.
If you do not plan early,
later you will regret it like Qí 齊.
Will you be able to plan then?
If you plan now,
this is the time."
The Marquis of Dèng 鄧侯 said:
"People will not eat my leftovers."
He replied,
"If you do not listen to the three ministers,
then the altars of the state will indeed not receive sacrifices,
and from where will you, the ruler, obtain any surplus?"
He did not listen.
The following year,
the Chǔ ruler attacked Dèng.
In the sixteenth year,
Chǔ again attacked Dèng,
and destroyed it.

B3.8.1 In the spring of the eighth year,
drilling troops at the ancestral temple
was proper.
B3.8.2 In summer,
our army and the Qí army besieged Chéng.
Chéng surrendered to the Qí army.
Zhòng Qìngfǔ requested to attack the Qí army.
The Duke said,
"It is not permissible.
Truly, I lack virtue.
What crime has the Qí army committed?
The fault lies with me.
The *Xià Shū* says,
'Gāoyáo diligently cultivated virtue,
when there is virtue,
then blessings descend.'
Let us diligently cultivate virtue
and await the time!"
In autumn,
the army returned.
Therefore, gentlemen praised Duke Zhuāng of Lǔ for this.
B3.8.3 The Marquis of Qí sent Lián Chēng and
Guǎn Zhìfù to garrison Kuíqiū,
going when the melons ripened,
saying:
"Replace them when the melons ripen."
The time for the garrison arrived,
but the duke inquired and they had not arrived.
They requested to be replaced,
but were not permitted.
Therefore, they plotted to rebel.
Duke Xī's younger brother was named Yí Zhòngnián,
who had a grandson named Gōngsūn Wúzhī,
who was favored by Duke Xī,
and whose clothing and ceremonial rank were like that of the heir apparent.
Duke Xiāng demoted him.
The two men (Lián Chēng and Guǎn Zhìfù) used this as a reason to rebel.
Lián Chēng had a younger sister in the duke's palace,
who was not favored.
He sent her to spy on the duke,
saying:
"If you succeed,
I will make you the wife of the duke."
In the twelfth month of winter,
the Marquis of Qí was traveling in Gūfén,
and then hunting in Bèiqiū.
He saw a large pig.
An attendant said,
"It is Gōngzǐ Péngshēng."
The duke was angry
and said,
"Péngshēng dares to appear!"
He shot at it.
The pig stood on its hind legs and squealed.
The duke was frightened
and fell from the chariot.
He injured his foot
and lost his shoe.
Upon returning, he demanded the shoe from the attendant Fèi.
Unable to find it,
he whipped him
until he bled.
Fèi ran out
and encountered a robber at the gate.
He was seized and bound.
Fèi said,
"What can I use to defend myself?"
He bared his back to show them.
They believed him.
Fèi requested to enter first.
He hid the duke and went out,
fought,
and died in the doorway.
Shí zhī Fēnrú died beneath the steps.
Then he entered and
killed Mèng Yáng 孟陽 on the bed.
He said,
"This is not the lord;
he doesn't resemble him."
Seeing Duke Xiāng's 襄公 feet under the door,
he then murdered him
and installed Wú Zhī 無知.
Initially,
when Duke Xiāng 襄公 came to power,
he lacked constancy.
Bào Shūyá 鮑叔牙 said,
"The lord causes the people to be negligent;
disorder will arise."
He escorted Gōngzǐ Xiǎobái 公子小白, the son of the duke, to flee to Jǔ 莒.
When the disorder arose,
Guǎn Yíwú 管夷吾 and Zhào Hū 召忽 escorted Gōngzǐ Jiū 公子糾 to come and seek refuge.
B3.8.4 Initially,
Gōngsūn Wúzhī 公孫無知 was cruel to Yōng Lǐn 雍廩.

A3.10 *The Tenth Year of Duke Zhuāng*
A3.10.1 In the tenth year, in spring,
in the first month of the king,
the duke defeated the Qí army at Chángsháo.
A3.10.2 In the second month,
the Duke attacked Sòng.
A3.10.3 In the third month,
the people of Sòng moved Sù.
A3.10.4 In the summer, the sixth month,
the Qí army and

A3.10.5 In the autumn, the ninth month,
Jīng defeated the Cài army at Shēn,
and took Hóu Wǔ of Cài back as a captive.
A3.10.6 In the winter, the tenth month,
the Qí army extinguished Tán.

B3.10 *Zuāng Gōng, Year Ten, Commentary*
B3.10.1 In the spring of the tenth year,
the Qí army attacked us.
The Duke was about to fight.
Cáo Guì requested an audience.
His fellow villagers said:
"Those who eat meat (the nobles) plan it;
what business is it of yours?"
Guì said:
"Those who eat meat are base
and unable to plan for the distant future."
Thereupon he went in to see the Duke
and asked how to fight.
The Duke said:
"The comfort of clothing and food
I do not dare to monopolize;
I always share with others."
Guì answered:
"Small favors do not extend everywhere;
the people will not follow you."
The Duke said:
"Sacrificial animals and jade and silk
I dare not increase;
I always use them with sincerity."
Guì answered:
"Small sincerity does not inspire confidence;
the spirits will not bless you."
The Duke said:
"In large and small lawsuits,
even though I cannot examine them thoroughly,
I always deal with them according to the facts."
Guì answered:
"This is a matter of loyalty,
and you can fight on that basis.
If you fight,
then please allow me to follow."
The Duke rode in the same chariot with him.
They fought at Chángsháo.
The Duke was about to beat the drum.
Guì said:
"Not yet."
The Qí people beat the drum three times.
Guì said:
"Now you may!"
The Qí army was utterly defeated.
The Duke was about to pursue them.
Guì said:
"Not yet."
He got down
and examined their wheel tracks,
then mounted the carriage bar and looked out at them,
saying:
"Now you may!"
Thereupon they pursued the Qí army.
After they had won,
the Duke asked him the reason.
He replied:
"In battle, courage is everything.
The first drumbeat rouses the troops' courage,
the second diminishes it,
and the third exhausts it.
When their courage was exhausted and ours was full,
therefore we defeated them.
Moreover, a large state
It is difficult to fathom,
I feared there was an ambush.
I saw that their wheel tracks were disordered,
I observed that their flags were falling,
therefore I pursued them."
B3.10.2 In the sixth month of summer,
the Qí 齊 army and the Sòng 宋 army were stationed at Láng 郎.
Gōngzǐ Yǎn 公子偃 said:
"The Sòng 宋 army is not well-disciplined,
it can be defeated.
If Sòng 宋 is defeated,
Qí 齊 will surely return.
I request to attack them."
The Duke did not permit it.
He secretly went out from the Yú Mén 雩門,
covered in tiger skin and charged ahead to attack them.
The Duke followed him,
and greatly defeated the Sòng 宋 army at Chéngqiū 乘丘.
The Qí 齊 army then returned.
B3.10.3 Marquis Āi of Cài 蔡哀侯 married a woman from Chén 陳,
Marquis Xī 息侯 also married her.
As Lady Xī Guī 息媯 was returning [to her husband's state],
she passed through Cài 蔡.
The Marquis of Cài 蔡 said:
"She is my wife's sister."
He stopped her and met with her,
but did not treat her as a guest.
Marquis Xī 息侯 heard of this,
Enraged,
he sent word to King Wén of Chǔ, saying:
"If you attack me,
I will seek aid from Cài and then attack them."
The Chǔ ruler followed his advice.
In the ninth month of autumn,
Chǔ defeated the Cài army at Shēn,
and returned with the Marquis of Cài, Xiàn Wǔ, as a captive.
B3.10.4 When the Marquis of Qí was leaving,
he passed through Tán,
but Tán did not treat him with proper courtesy.
And when he returned,
all the lords offered congratulations,
but Tán still did not come.
In winter,
the Qí army destroyed Tán,
because Tán was disrespectful.
The ruler of Tán fled to Jǔ,
due to their former alliance.
A3.11 *Annals of the Eleventh Year of Duke Zhuāng*
A3.11.1 In the eleventh year, spring,
the king's first month.
A3.11.2 In summer, the fifth month,
on the day wù-yín,
the Duke defeated the Sòng army at Zī.

B3.11 *Commentary on the Eleventh Year of Zhuāng Gōng*
B3.11.1 In the summer of the eleventh year,
Sòng, because of the incident at Chéngqiū,
invaded us.
The Duke defended against them.
The Sòng army had not yet formed ranks when we pressed them,
defeating them at Zī.
In all military matters,
if the enemy has not formed ranks, it is called
"defeating a certain army";
if they have all formed ranks, it is called "battle";
a great collapse is called "a crushing defeat."
Capturing leaders is called "a victory";
utterly defeating them is called "capturing a certain army";
if the capital's army is defeated, it is called
"the King's army suffered a crushing defeat at such-and-such place."
B3.11.2 In autumn,
Sòng was flooded.
The Duke sent someone to express condolences,
saying:
"Heaven sends excessive rain,
He was harmed by the sacrificial offerings.
How can he not be pitied?"
He replied,
"Indeed, I, the orphaned one, was disrespectful.
Heaven sent down this disaster,
and I further caused worry for the ruler.
I accept the disgrace of the commission."
Zāng Wénzhòng 曰:
"Sòng is probably going to rise!
Yǔ and Tāng blamed themselves for their faults,
and their rise was swift.
Jié and Zhòu blamed others,
and their fall was sudden.
Moreover, when a state has misfortune,
to call oneself 'the orphaned one'
is proper.
He speaks with fear and acts with propriety,
Qí shù hū!”
Shortly afterwards, it was heard that:
“This is the speech of Gōngzǐ Yùyuē.”
Zāngsūn Dá said:
“He is fit to be the ruler,
he has a heart that cares for the people.”
B3.11.3 In winter,
the Marquis of Qí came to welcome Gòng Jī.
B3.11.4 In the Battle of Chéngqiū,
the Duke used the gold púgū to shoot Nángōng Chángwàn,
the Duke's right-hand man Zhuǎn Sūnshēng grappled with him.
The people of Sòng requested him.
Duke of Sòng begrudged him,
saying:
“At first, I respected you;
now you
are a prisoner of Lǔ,

the people within the country,

That I have no disloyal intentions
This is Heaven's decree.

Harmonious sounds, clang clang.

none will compare to his capital.'"
Duke Lì of Chén,
came from Cài,
therefore, the people of Cài killed Wǔ Fǔ

When he was young,

he obtained "Contemplation" ䷓ changing to "Obstruction" ䷋,

Light,
is far away and shines from elsewhere.

A courtyard filled with a hundred troops,

"It is beneficial to be a guest at the royal court."
It still has observation,
therefore it is said that it is in the rear!

Jiāng
is the descendant of Dàyuè.
Mountains and great peaks are paired with heaven.

When Chén 衰 (shuāi) declines,
will this be its flourishing?"

decline.

is for promoting virtue.

therefore it was delayed.
B5.8.5 Duke Sòng was ill;
Crown Prince Zīfù earnestly requested,
saying:
"[Mù Yí] is mature and benevolent,
Your Lordship should establish him!"
The Duke ordered Zǐ Yú.
Zǐ Yú declined,
saying:
"To be able to yield the state,
what benevolence is greater than that?
Your servant is not up to it,
moreover, it is also not compliant."
Thereupon, he ran away and withdrew.

A5.9.1 In the ninth year, in spring,
in the third month, on the day *dīngchǒu*,
Duke Yù Shuō of Sòng died.
A5.9.2 In summer,
the Duke met with the Steward Zhōu Gōng,
the Marquis of Qí,
the Viscount of Sòng,
the Marquis of Wèi,
the Count of Zhèng,
the Viscount of Xǔ,

A5.9.3 In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day *yǐyǒu*,
Bó Jī died.
A5.9.4 In the ninth month, on the day wùchén,
the lords made a covenant at Kuíqiū.
A5.9.5 On the day jiǎzǐ,

B5.9 *Commentary on the Ninth Year of Duke Xī*
B5.9.1 In the ninth year, in spring,
Duke Huán of Sòng died.
Before he was buried, Duke Xiāng convened the lords,
therefore he is referred to as "
zi (son)".
Generally, during mourning,
the king is called "
xiǎo tóng (little child)",
and dukes and marquises are called "
zi (son)".
B5.9.2 In summer,
they met at Kuíqiū
to renew the covenant
and cultivate good relations,
which is proper etiquette.
The king sent Zǎi Kǒng
to bestow blessed meat upon the Marquis of Qí,
He said:
"The Son of Heaven has affairs related to Wén
and Wǔ,
and sent Kǒng to bestow the sacrificial meat upon your maternal uncle."
The Lord of Qí was about to descend and bow.
Kǒng said:
"There is yet a further command.
The Son of Heaven sent Kǒng, saying:
'Because your maternal uncle is old and advanced in years,
and greatly burdened,
he is granted an additional grade [of honor],
without the need to descend and bow!'"
He replied:
"The majesty of Heaven is never far from one's face, even at a short distance.
Xiǎo Bái,
how dare I covet the Son of Heaven's command
and not descend and bow?
- I fear falling and stumbling below,
and thus bringing shame upon the Son of Heaven.
How dare I not descend and bow?"
He descended,
and bowed;
ascended [the platform],
and received [the sacrificial meat].
B5.9.3 In autumn,
the Lord of Qí convened the feudal lords in a covenant at Kuíqiū,
saying:
"All those who are allied with us,
After the alliance,
they said, "Let's return to being on good terms."
Zǎi Kǒng returned first,
and met the Marquis of Jìn,
saying:
"It is permissible not to attend the meeting.
The Marquis of Qí does not focus on virtue
but is diligent in far-reaching strategies,
therefore he has campaigned north against the Shān Róng,
south against Chǔ,
and now has created this western meeting.
We do not know his eastern strategies,
but the western ones are clear.
He is probably creating chaos!
Your Lordship should focus on pacifying the chaos,
and not be diligent in travel."
The Marquis of Jìn then returned.
B5.9.4 In the ninth month,
the Duke Xiàn of Jìn died.
Lì Kè and Pī Zhèng wanted to install Duke Wén,
and therefore used the followers of the three sons of the Duke to create chaos.
Initially,
Duke Xiàn made Xún Xī the tutor of Xī Qí.
The Duke fell ill,
and summoned him,
saying:
"To entrust these young orphans and disgrace them before the grandees,
what is to be done?"
He bowed his head and replied,
"Your servant will exhaust the strength of his arms and legs,
and add to it loyalty
and integrity.
If it succeeds,
it is due to your Majesty's spirit;
if it fails,
then I will follow it with my death."
The Duke said,
"What is meant by loyalty
and integrity?"
He replied,
"The benefit of the ducal house,
knowing it and doing everything without fail,
is loyalty;
attending to the dead and serving the living,
in pairs without any suspicion,
is integrity."
When Lì Kè was about to kill Xī Qí,
he first told Xún Xī, saying,
"The three resentments are about to arise,
with Qín and Jìn assisting them.
What will you do?"
Xún Xī said,
"I will die for it."
Lì Kè said,
"It will be of no benefit."
Xún Shū said,
"I have already spoken with the late lord,"
"it cannot be changed."
"Does he wish to speak again and yet cherish his own life?
Even though it is of no benefit,
where could he escape to?
Moreover, in the desire for goodness,
who is not like me?
I desire to be unwavering,
and can I say that others have already done so?"
In the tenth month of winter,
Lì Kè killed Xī Qí at the encampment.
The record says
"killed the son of the ruler,"
as he had not yet been buried.
Xún Xī was about to die for it,
and someone said:
"It would be better to install Zhuō Zǐ
and assist him."
Xún Xī installed Gōngzǐ Zhuō
in order to bury (Xī Qí).
In the eleventh month,
Lì Kè killed Gōngzǐ Zhuō at court.
Xún Xī died for it.
The gentleman said:
"The *Poetry* says
'A flaw in white jade
can still be ground away;
but a flaw in these words
"It cannot be done."
Xún Xī 荀息 had them."
B5.9.5 The Marquis of Qí 齊, with the army of the various lords, attacked Jìn 晉,
reaching Gāoliáng 高梁 and then returning,
to punish the disorder in Jìn 晉.
The order did not reach Lǔ 魯,
therefore it was not recorded.
B5.9.6 Xì Ruì 郤芮 of Jìn 晉 sent Yíwú 夷吾 with heavy bribes to Qín 秦
to seek entry,
saying:
"If someone truly possesses a state,
why should I begrudge it?
If he can govern the people upon entry,
what ownership does the land truly hold?"
He followed this advice.
Xí Péng 隰朋 of Qí 齊 led an army to meet the Qín 秦 army
to install Duke Huì of Jìn 晉.
The Earl of Qín 秦 said to Xì Ruì 郤芮:
"Who does the lord rely on?"
He replied:
"I have heard
that a fugitive has no party,
and if he has a party, he must have enemies.
Yíwú 夷吾 is weak and does not like playing around,
his ability to fight is unremarkable,
and he will not change even when he grows up.
I do not know anything else about him."
The Duke said to Gōngsūn Zhī 公孫枝:
"Yí Wú will he be settled?"
He replied:
"Your servant has heard it said:
'Only the principles will settle the state.'
The *Shī* (Book of Odes) says:
'Not knowing, not understanding,
Obeying the principles of the Emperor.'
This refers to King Wén."
"It also says:
'Neither presumptuous nor thieving,
Seldom is one not a principle.'
Having neither likes nor dislikes,
Neither jealous nor conquering is what it means.
Now his words are full of jealousy and conquering,
Difficult indeed!"
The duke said:
"Jealousy begets much resentment,
How can he conquer then?
This is to my advantage."
B5.9.7 Duke Xiāng of Sòng ascended the throne.
Considering Gōngzǐ Mùyí to be benevolent,
he made him Left Preceptor to listen to government affairs.
Thereupon Sòng was well-governed.
Therefore, the Yú lineage served as Left Preceptors for generations.

B5.10 *Commentary on the Tenth Year of Duke Xī*
B5.10.1 Tenth year, spring,
the Dí destroyed Wēn because
Sū Zǐ was untrustworthy.
Sū Zǐ betrayed the King and allied with the Dí,
yet was unable to be loyal to the Dí,
so the Dí people attacked him.
The King did not rescue him,
therefore it was destroyed.
Sū Zǐ fled to Wèi.
B5.10.2 In the fourth month of summer,
Zhōu Gōng Jìfù and
Wángzǐ Dǎng met with Qí Xīpéng
to install the Marquis of Jìn.
The Marquis of Jìn killed Lǐkè
to appease (the people).
As he was about to kill Lǐkè,
the Duke sent a message to him, saying:
"Without you,
I would not have reached this point.
However,
you killed two rulers and one high official;
for one who is your lord,
isn't that difficult?"
He replied:
"If there were no deposed rulers,
how would the lord rise?
If you want to condemn someone,
is there any need for words?
I have received my fate."
He lay on his sword and died.
Thereupon, Pī Zhèng was sent as an envoy to Qín,
and also apologized for the slow delivery of gifts,
therefore he did not arrive in time.

Encountered the Dàzǐ (太子).
